- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in next period; apply downward correction of 5–10% for 1–2 periods post-spike.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods, consider adding 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward recent highs.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 30d average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.40” values, model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast to catch upward momentum.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often fails to react quickly; forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–5% in first 3–5 days of sentiment change.
